workPackageTitle: Import accepted gameplay catalogs into initial JSON definitions
notes: Entries are added before implementation and are never renumbered (docs/technical/91 § Verification registry).

DAT-007 has no implementation. content/README.md states it plainly: the tree is JSON transcribed by hand ahead of DAT-007, DAT-001 through DAT-006 do not exist, and 'this tree cannot be its completion'. This file therefore registers what is verifiable about that prepared tree TODAY, by the one thing that exists to verify it - the stdlib-only checker at src/MechaMiner.Tools/ContentImport/verify_content.py - and not the package's own gate, which is 'totals/mappings/numbers match GDD/CSV reports' over an importer that has not been written (docs/technical/110-implementation-plan-for-ai-agents.md:216).

The selector is a Python script rather than a test ID because no test project exists on this branch. When the importer lands, these entries are superseded by importer coverage rather than deleted, and the checker's assertion keeps its VER ID: doc 91 forbids renumbering, and an interim gate that was real is not a tombstone just because a better one replaced it.

VER-DAT-007-001 exists because the assertion it covers was FALSE for a population nobody chose. A21 counted every *.json under content/ and compared it to 139, while NON_DEFINITION_DIRS in the same file already named 'localization' and 'schemas' as directories that are not catalogs of definitions. The two halves of that contradiction were never reconciled, so the row was correct only for as long as content/schemas/ stayed absent - and it is doc 40 § Accepted content repository layout's first declared directory. The defect surfaced as a false failure charged to another branch, which is the shape this registry exists to make expensive.

What the control set is chosen to exclude, stated because a single injection would have looked adequate: the excluded-directory injection alone is satisfied by deleting the assertion outright, and the catalog-directory injection alone is satisfied by the bare enumeration that was already there. Only the pair distinguishes 'counts the right population' from 'counts' and from 'does not count'. The third injection is the regression guard on the fix itself - narrowing a population is the obvious way to also narrow a row's reach by accident, so a definition in a declared directory that no A12 row covers must still fail.

One enumeration under content/ deliberately does NOT honour NON_DEFINITION_DIRS and is not a defect: A26 (check_no_nulls). 'No null anywhere under content/' is a whole-tree claim, and content/localization/en.json is named in the ContentImport README as covered there on purpose. It carries a measured consequence for DAT-006 rather than a predicted one: a probe schema containing {"properties":{"presentation_id":{"default":null}}} fails A26 as '...probe.schema.json.properties.presentation_id.default'. JSON Schema authors nulls legally, so the first content/schemas/*.json to use one will redden A26, and the resolution is a scope decision for whoever lands the schemas. It is recorded here, and in a docstring at the assertion, so that it is not discovered as a surprise and not silently absorbed into an exception set - which is the one remedy A26's own docstring rules out.

VER-DAT-007-001 is registered at tier 'fast' and is reached by NOTHING. That is a wiring gap rather than a gate defect, and it is recorded here because this entry is the only artifact on master that knows the gate exists. Measured on master 2e1abca: no ./build.sh or ./build.ps1 exists, so the verb wrappers doc 100 s Standard command surface specifies are absent; build/ holds exactly three verify-*.sh scripts and not one of them mentions verify_content.py or ContentImport at all; .github is absent from master at every path; and nothing anywhere reads this registry and executes a selector. The executed gate set is therefore a hand-kept list - verify-policies, verify-architecture, verify-godot, restore, build - and this selector is the one of the registry's six distinct selectors that sits outside it. The consequence is already on the record: merge 54527f8 added content/.gitkeep, was certified green by every gate that ran, and left this gate red on master from that merge until the file was deleted, while an unrelated pull request was the thing that appeared to have broken it.

WHERE THE WIRING MUST GO, for whoever owns the verb. The verb is 'test-fast': doc 100 s Standard command surface defines it as 'pure bounded tests, content validation, representative headless fixtures', and 'content validation' is this selector. The secondary home is the 'content' verb, which subsumes this checker once DAT-006's importer exists; until then test-fast is the one that must call it. It is deliberately NOT wired from master. ./build.sh and build/verify-gate-wiring.sh are both owned by the FND-002 stream and already exist on that chain - twelve build/*.sh scripts there against master's four - so a competing wrapper added here would collide with the dispatcher that is about to arrive; and by verify-gate-wiring.sh's own property 4, that 'reached' means reached from a workflow, a call site on a branch with no .github would not be wired in any case. Two things must happen at the merge where master's ContentImport scripts arrive on that chain, and that gate is designed to stay red until they do. First, its INVENTORY must classify FOUR .py files under src/MechaMiner.Tools/ContentImport/, not three: the comment there names check_quote_mismatch_evidence.py, derive_citation_pass_expectations.py and verify_content.py, and omits derive_derived_value_expectations.py, which is 75306 bytes on master and carries both a .py extension and a shebang, so both of that gate's enumerators see it. Second, verify_content.py must be classified as a gate reached from test-fast rather than exempted. Two figures in that file's FOLLOW-UP are also stale as measured here: verify_content.py is 232139 bytes, not 132 KB, and the trailing-whitespace repair it prices at 74 lines across three files now costs zero - all four files have no trailing-whitespace line, no CRLF and a final newline - so adding '.py' to OwnedTextHygiene.OwnedExtensions no longer reddens format-check on master's copies.

entries.summary: A21's file inventory counts the definition population - every *.json under content/ except those beneath a NON_DEFINITION_DIRS directory - and what establishes that is a pair of opposite injections, not the green run. Adding content/schemas/envelope.schema.json together with a content/schemas/README.md leaves the verdict at PASS and exit 0; adding one definition under content/relics/ moves it to FAIL and exit 1 with 'content/ holds 139 definition *.json file(s), expected 138'. Neither half proves anything alone. The first is satisfied by an assertion that was deleted, and the second is satisfied by the bare CONTENT.rglob('*.json') this replaced, which counted content/localization/en.json into the definition total and so reported 'content/ holds 140 *.json file(s), expected 139' for the first schema authored under a directory the checker itself already classified as not a catalog of definitions. A third injection guards the fix rather than the original defect: a definition under content/presentation/, a directory doc 40 declares and no A12 row covers, must still FAIL with the count, because narrowing the population is the obvious way to accidentally narrow the row's reach at the same time. The expectation was rebased from 139 onto the definition population's true size (138) rather than raised to 140, which would have made the row green by agreeing with the polluted population. All three of those injections are negative controls, and that is recorded here rather than in `evidenceKinds`: a negative control is how a gate was built, not what it emitted, and what these three emit is an exit code and a stdout row, which are the two kinds the entry already declares. Listing the technique as a third kind would omit no evidence but inflate the coverage the field appears to report.
